analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sassuolo sacked Alberto Aquilani on 9 November after five straight league defeats, the last a 3-0 loss at Roma, and they have the worst defence in Serie A with 29 conceded in 11 games. Their new coach had not been named in the reports I read, with Roberto D'Aversa linked, so they may be a few games into a new set-up by this trip. Eusebio Di Francesco's Lecce are a crowded treatment room, with Ilic and Pierotti out long term after surgery.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Sassuolo's leaky defence argues for more, but a new coach usually starts by tightening up, and Lecce are without the creativity of Pierotti and Ilic, so these roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Nothing in the news moves this; Lecce at home should take most of them, which fits the site's 5.5 to 3.9 split.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean slightly higher because both clubs sit near the drop zone, and a Sassuolo side fighting to end a long losing run under new management is likely to play an edgy game. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots, with 16.4 for Lecce. I lean a little lower: Lecce are missing Pierotti and Ilic, and Monteiro has also had a calf tear, which takes away a good share of their attacking threat.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Lecce's absences point down and Sassuolo's weak defence points up, so I stay with the site's number.
